content: Sodium bicarbonate interacts with various medications and substances, primarily by altering gastric pH or renal tubular reabsorption. Below is a detailed explanation of its interactions and potential effects: 1. Sodium bicarbonate and aspirin (rectal or oral): Sodium bicarbonate increases the pH, which affects the passive renal tubular reabsorption of salicylates. At moderate doses, salicylate levels may increase, while at higher doses, levels decrease due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 2. Sodium bicarbonate and atazanavir: Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which affects its solubility and absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. 3. Sodium bicarbonate and atenolol: Sodium bicarbonate decreases atenolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. It is recommended to separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 4. Sodium bicarbonate and azithromycin: Sodium bicarbonate reduces azithromycin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 5. Sodium bicarbonate and balsalazide: Sodium bicarbonate increases the pH, which may affect the renal tubular reabsorption of salicylates. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion. The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Sodium bicarbonate and benazepril: Sodium bicarbonate may reduce the effects of benazepril through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Sodium bicarbonate and beta-blockers (e.g., betaxolol, bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol, nadolol, nebivolol, propranolol, timolol): Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of these beta-blockers by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 8. Sodium bicarbonate and antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, gemifloxacin, ofloxacin): Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of these antibiotics by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and separate administration by 2 hours. Monitor for potential crystalluria and nephrotoxicity with ciprofloxacin due to decreased solubility in alkaline urine. 9. Sodium bicarbonate and iron supplements (e.g., ferrous sulfate, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferric maltol): Sodium bicarbonate decreases the absorption of iron supplements by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 10. Sodium bicarbonate and antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole): Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of these antifungals by increasing gastric pH, which affects their solubility and absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Sodium bicarbonate and ACE inhibitors (e.g., captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, trandolapril): Sodium bicarbonate may reduce the effects of these medications through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Sodium bicarbonate and tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline, oxytetracycline, sarecycline, tetracycline): Sodium bicarbonate decreases the absorption of tetracyclines by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and separate administration by 2 hours. 13. Sodium bicarbonate and salicylates (e.g., salsalate, willow bark): Sodium bicarbonate increases the pH, which affects the renal tubular reabsorption of salicylates. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion. The clinical significance is unclear. 14. Sodium bicarbonate and digoxin: Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Sodium bicarbonate and diuretics or corticosteroids: Sodium bicarbonate may exacerbate hypokalemia when used with these agents. Monitor potassium levels closely. 16. Sodium bicarbonate and lactulose: Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of lactulose by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Sodium bicarbonate and memantine: Sodium bicarbonate increases memantine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Sodium bicarbonate and sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol: Both agents can decrease serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Sodium bicarbonate and quinidine: Sodium bicarbonate increases quinidine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Elevated quinidine levels may lead to cardiac conduction disturbances and arrhythmias. Monitor closely. 20. Sodium bicarbonate and rose hips: Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Monitor closely. 21. Sodium bicarbonate and ursodiol: Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of ursodiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 22. Sodium bicarbonate and zoledronic acid: Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Adverse Effects and Precautions: Sodium bicarbonate can cause metabolic alkalosis, hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, hypernatremia, and edema. Intravenous administration may lead to fluid overload, dilution of serum electrolytes, and pulmonary edema. Use with caution in patients with congestive heart failure, renal insufficiency, hypertension, or sodium-retaining states. Avoid in children with diabetic ketoacidosis and in patients on concurrent corticosteroid therapy. Monitor for milk-alkali syndrome, cerebral hemorrhage, and tetany in susceptible individuals. This information highlights the importance of careful monitoring and dose adjustments when sodium bicarbonate is used concomitantly with other medications.
